before.title: Demand pattern
before.body: Delta Hotels demand follows market seasonality plus Bonvoy campaign calendars. Treat portfolio averages as directional only until property pace data exists.

before.title: Competitive pressure
before.body: Same-market Marriott sister brands can both help (Bonvoy shoppers) and cannibalize. Map sister-brand density before assuming exclusive Bonvoy capture for Delta Hotels.

before.title: Conversion workstream
before.body: Systems, content, and rate integrity at cutover determine whether platform demand actually books the hotel in week one.

before.title: What is differentiated commercially
before.body: Canadian-inspired upper-upscale full-service brand emphasizing genuine hospitality and uncluttered design inside Marriott International / Marriott Bonvoy. Commercially, the brand case is Bonvoy + Marriott channels applied to a distinct Delta Hotels product — not a generic Marriott International story.

before.title: Commercial engine
before.body: Delta Hotels by Marriott sells through Marriott International distribution and Marriott Bonvoy while the brand product must still win the stay. Commercial diligence should separate platform reach from Delta Hotels conversion on the property.

after.title: Commercial Engine
after.body: Delta Hotels by Marriott commercial distribution rides Marriott Bonvoy direct channels, GDS, OTAs, and parent sales systems. Upscale productive full-service: efficient meetings, thoughtful F&B, and Bonvoy for travelers and groups who want upscale utility with conversion-friendly pathways. Owners should underwrite channel mix and loyalty contribution for this asset—not corporate averages alone.
